pages.text: Some things only age in the right weather. Dirt turns to mud, a sponge soaks, and an empty bottle or bucket fills only $(l)in the rain$(), with the kiln out under the sky. Kelp, wet sponges and petals dry, and clay bakes to brick, only $(l)by day, under a clear sky$(). Ink takes on a glow only $(l)under the night sky$().$(br2)When the weather is wrong the wait stands still, keeping the days it already has. Ask the kiln and it says what it is waiting for.

pages.title: Other places
pages.text: Some recipes belong to one dimension, and there they come first. In $(l)the Nether$() cobblestone darkens to blackstone and sand to soul sand, five days each. In $(l)the End$() obsidian begins to weep in seven days, and chorus fruit pops in two.
